title: the decrypt loop reads six bytes past its packet-scope chunk into the next chunk of the same block
live_proof: LIVE, read two-sided from the pinned tree. The vulnerable read is present at v4.6.8:epan/dissectors/packet-solaredge.c:1029 -- 'out[i] = intermediate_decrypted_payload[i + 6] ^ intermediate_decrypted_payload[2+(i&3)];' inside 'for (i = 0; i < payload_length; i++)' -- and the fix's marker 'payload_length -= 6' has ZERO occurrences in the pinned file. The two chunks are allocated at :1007 and :1008, both wmem_alloc(scratch, payload_length), and scratch is pinfo->pool at the :1292 call site. The pin additionally has no guard on `length` at all, so payload_length can go negative; that is a SECOND defect in the same function and is not what this case claims.
object: the intermediate decrypted payload, payload_length bytes in the packet scope
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. Spatial row: the cursor leaves the chunk.
shape: loop reads a fixed offset past its chunk into the next chunk of the same block
allocator_layer: block_fast -- the packet scope (pinfo->pool). In this harness the bound that fires is wm_narrow()'s per-allocation shrink, not the chunk adapter's.
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. The decrypt arithmetic is reduced to the loop's LAST read, index payload_length - 1 + 6, which is the one that leaves the chunk; the cipher calls are dropped because they do not touch the bound.

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O0; wmem and the port built with the same flags). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 402653184` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 402653184` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (b64cd18b85d0); the arm was previously 'declined'.
native-detect.note: DECLINED, not pending, and the reason is a measurement rather than an estimate: the two-sided shape is already established by the FFmpeg sub-object probe (ffmpeg/subobject-repros/results/20261005-native-subobject/asan-probe.c), where the member-to-member crossing draws NO report while a write one element past the whole allocation draws heap-buffer-overflow. Every crossing in this corpus stays inside one g_malloc'd block or slab page by the same mechanism, so eight more silent-with-control runs would confirm what one already showed. Two further reasons not to spend them: the wireshark corpus has no standalone native build to instrument, and the memcached one would have to instrument the case while linking an uninstrumented port library -- the mixed mode in which that probe's own -O1 artefact arose, where BOTH arms went silent because the dead stores were optimised away. If this arm is ever wanted, it needs its positive control in the same binary.
native-detect.prediction: NO ASan report: the crossing stays inside the one g_malloc'd block, so there is no redzone between the chunks to poison. A silent arm needs its own positive control -- a crossing past the END of the block, which ASan must report -- before it means anything.
